classification.difficultyReason: Coordinates elapsed times across different triathlon legs and compares sums of travel times.

content.prompt: In a triathlon event, two competitors, Alan and Shen, are keen rivals. The event consists of an 800 m swim, a 50 km bicycle ride and a 20 km run. Alan can swim at 2 km/h, cycle at 35 km/h and run at 10 km/h (all average speeds). Shen can swim at 2.4 km/h, cycle at 30 km/h and run at 12 km/h (all average speeds). Assume no time is lost when transitioning between legs.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the distance between Shen and Alan when Alan has completed the swim.

answer.worked:
The swim is $0.8$ km. Alan's swimming time is $\frac{0.8}{2}=\frac25$ h, and Shen's swimming time is $\frac{0.8}{2.4}=\frac13$ h.

When Alan finishes swimming, Shen has been cycling for
$$\begin{align*}t&=\frac25-\frac13\\t&=\frac1{15}\text{ h}.\end{align*}$$
Shen's cycling distance is
$$\begin{align*}d&=30\times\frac1{15}\\d&=2\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$
Alan is at the end of the swim, so Shen is 2 km ahead.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find which of the two competitors finishes first, and the difference between their times, to the nearest minute.

answer.short: Shen finishes first by approximately 10 minutes.
answer.worked:
Using $\text{time}=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}$, Alan's total time is
$$\begin{align*}T_A&=\frac{0.8}{2}+\frac{50}{35}+\frac{20}{10}\\T_A&=\frac25+\frac{10}{7}+2\\T_A&=\frac{134}{35}\text{ h}.\end{align*}$$
Shen's total time is
$$\begin{align*}T_S&=\frac{0.8}{2.4}+\frac{50}{30}+\frac{20}{12}\\T_S&=\frac13+\frac53+\frac53\\T_S&=\frac{11}{3}\text{ h}.\end{align*}$$
The difference is
$$\begin{align*}T_A-T_S&=\frac{134}{35}-\frac{11}{3}\\T_A-T_S&=\frac{17}{105}\text{ h}.\end{align*}$$
In minutes, $\frac{17}{105}\times60=\frac{68}{7}$, which rounds to 10 minutes. Shen finishes first.
